title: Latency signature correlation — standup notes
content:
Meeting: Performance sync — latency signature correlation (standing)
Date: 2026-10-30 (notes captured and edited through 2026-11-01)
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Daniel, Sofia, Marcus, Priya, two SRE on call (Ben, Elena)
Goal: Triage recurring tail-latency spikes we observed across model variants by correlating request \"signatures\" (input fingerprints) with kernel/runtime behavior and cache temperature.

Quick summary
- New observation: ~30% of tail spikes (p99-p999) on m-16b-int8 (dedicated pool) are associated with a small set (~7) of request prefixes (short structured prompts) that break our prefix-cache hit heuristic and trigger cold KV loads + slower kernel path selection.
- Hypothesis: prefix fingerprinting + interaction with batching heuristic causes these requests to be routed into single-request micro-batches that skip int8 fast path due to sequence-length variance. Secondary factor: kernel selector falls back to a conservative AVX kernel when quantized path mispredicts memory footprint.
- Immediate mitigation (short-term): increase prefix cache window + bias batching heuristic to prefer 2–4ms latency-increment but reduce singletons. Deployed as shadow policy in staging (experiment id: latency-sign-ep1).

Observed signals & data points
- Time window: 2026-10-24 -> 2026-10-29; clusters: eu-central-1-dedicated-gpupool-3
- Spike shape: sharp p999 jumps (2–6x baseline) lasting 10–90s; not tied to total QPS surge.
- Signature approach: we fingerprint inputs by normalized first 48 tokens (lowercased, removed user ids), hashed to 64-bit. Top 100 fingerprints covered ~82% of spikes; 7 fingerprints each responsible for single recurring spike pattern.
- Replay tests: synthetic replay of problematic fingerprints into a fresh worker reproduced p999 > baseline by 3.7x. When we primed KV cache with the same prefix (prewarm), p999 returned to baseline.
- Kernel switch logs: observed fallback to kernel_id 0x7b (conservative attention kernel) for sequences with high variance midbatch; this path has ~1.9x token latency vs fast int8 kernel 0x42.

Experiments run (brief)
- latency-sign-ep0 (A/B shadow): shadow routing to keep singletons queued till 2ms or until other requests arrive. Result: reduced singleton rate by 44%, p999 down ~18% for replays. Minor increase in median latency (+0.4ms). No customer-facing change.
- quant-fallthrough-check: toggled kernel selector aggressive score threshold down by 0.15 for 24h on one node. Reduced kernel fallbacks by 62% but caused an infrequent OOM in large-batched fusion jobs (tracked in PERF-1432).
- prefix-prewarm: instrumented controller to prewarm KV cache on detection of fingerprint seen > 3 times in 5m. Prewarm reduced p999 by ~60% for affected fingerprints in test cluster but increased memory pressure on that shard.

Hypotheses & root-cause threads
1) Signature-driven cache misses: small set of high-entropy prefixes produce poor cache reuse under our current prefix-merge window. Fix path: expand merge window for prefixes with high reuse probability OR implement micro-prefetch for detected signatures.
2) Batching / sequencing interaction: the batching heuristic places requests with similar signatures into micro-batches and then scheduling causes high variance in seq_len midbatch, triggering conservative kernels. Fix path: add sequence-length bucketing before kernel selection.
3) Kernel selector conservatism: current offline model for kernel memory estimate underestimates int8 memory pressure for some sequences; we need runtime probes to adjust threshold.

Action items (owner — ETA)
- Aisha: land a new lightweight signature prewarm controller prototype into staging (branch: feat/signature-prewarm). ETA: 2026-11-05.
- Daniel: instrument kernel selector logging to dump predicted vs actual mem usage for paths 0x42 and 0x7b for 72h on a canary node (node: eu-c-3-canary-01). ETA: 2026-11-03.
- Sofia: roll out shadow batching tweak to reduce singletons (latency-sign-ep1) to two more pools and collect QPS/latency deltas. ETA: 2026-11-02.
- Marcus: tie fingerprint set to a small persistent LRU of size 2048 to cap memory; implement metric: prefix-hotset-mem-bytes. ETA: 2026-11-08.
- Priya (SRE): monitor memory pressure on prewarm shards and add alert if prewarm cache > 70% of shard alloc. ETA: 2026-11-04.

Open questions / discussion notes
- How do we balance increasing merge window (which improves reuse) vs added latency for new unique requests? Trade-off: merge window at 3ms reduced p999 but raised median slightly.
- Should we make fingerprint detection model adaptive (ML-updated) or rule-based hotset? Quick wins prefer rule-based for simplicity, but long-term ML could adapt to workload drift.
- Could quantization profiles be tuned per-signature? (i.e., switch int8->int4 for highly repetitive prefixes). Complexity high; defer.

Quick troubleshooting checklist (for oncall)
- If you see p999 > 4x baseline and no QPS surge: run fingerprint-scan on warm traces (script: infra/tools/fingerprint_scan.py --window 60m)
- Check kernel fallbacks: grep kernel-fallback in /var/log/serving/kernel_selector.log and run the one-off probe (infra/probes/kernel_probe.sh --node <node> --model <model>)
- Prewarm verify: curl internal-admin/prewarm-status?shard=<shard_id> and check metric prefix_prewarm_hits{shard}

Notes to follow up (low priority)
- Explore prefix-aware quant profile mapping (longer project), link to PERF-1467 (product idea backlog)
- Add a weekly digest for the top 10 fingerprints causing regressions (automation idea)

Raw experiment outputs (snippets)
- replay run 2026-10-28 03:14 UTC: median=18.2ms p95=22.6ms p99=45.1ms p999=128.4ms
- replay with prewarm: median=18.6ms p95=22.3ms p99=25.9ms p999=32.1ms
- kernel-log sample: [2026-10-28T03:12:43Z] model=m-16b-int8 kernel_id=0x7b predicted_mem=7.9GB actual_mem=8.1GB seq_len_dist=[16,512,48]

References / links
- PERF ticket: PERF-1432 (kernel selector fallback investigation)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/918 (batching heuristics patch)
- Confluence: serving-runtime latency signature draft (see linked_artifacts)

Next sync: quick check-in 2026-11-03 (standup slot); longer retro/decisions on 2026-11-10.

Notes: informal, working doc — meant to capture runbook, experiments and next steps. Expect edits and follow-ups; if you want visibility add to collaborators or ping in #perf-bench-sync.
